title: Famine Campbell Commission
definition: The Campbell Commission (1866) was the first-ever famine commission appointed by the British Government in India, specifically tasked to investigate the causes and suggest relief measures following the devastating Orissa Famine of 1866.
importanceInUpsc: It marks the shift from 'laissez-faire' indifference to the formalization of 'Famine Codes' and state responsibility in disaster management, a recurring theme in Modern Indian History.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Famine Campbell Commission.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
